before.title: Demand pattern
before.body: Marriott Hotels demand follows market seasonality plus Bonvoy campaign calendars. Treat portfolio averages as directional only until property pace data exists.

before.title: Competitive pressure
before.body: Same-market Marriott sister brands can both help (Bonvoy shoppers) and cannibalize. Map sister-brand density before assuming exclusive Bonvoy capture for Marriott Hotels.

before.title: Conversion workstream
before.body: Systems, content, and rate integrity at cutover determine whether platform demand actually books the hotel in week one.

before.title: What is differentiated commercially
before.body: Core upper-upscale full-service Marriott flag for meetings-capable urban and suburban assets inside Marriott Bonvoy. Commercially, the brand case is Bonvoy + Marriott channels applied to a distinct Marriott Hotels product — not a generic Marriott International story.

before.title: Commercial engine
before.body: Marriott Hotels sells through Marriott International distribution and Marriott Bonvoy while the brand product must still win the stay. Commercial diligence should separate platform reach from Marriott Hotels conversion on the property.

after.title: Commercial Engine
after.body: Marriott Hotels commercial distribution rides Marriott Bonvoy direct channels, GDS, OTAs, and parent sales systems. Full-service upscale flagship: meetings, F&B, and Bonvoy for travelers and groups expecting classic Marriott Hotels service intensity. Owners should underwrite channel mix and loyalty contribution for this asset—not corporate averages alone.
